director.chapterArc: Tactical briefing to confrontation, shifting from Rook's authoritative command to Toren's desperate intervention and final realization of the creature's mechanics.
director.restraintNote: Maintain clinical precision during technical descriptions; allow silence to carry the weight of injury and fear rather than vocalizing it. The shift from Rook's flat delivery to Toren's rising intensity must be earned through pacing, not volume.

cues.delivery: Rook's briefing is a flat, tactical recitation of facts. No rising inflection for emphasis; treat the 'forty seconds' as a cold inventory.
cues.from: "Everything I know about a Barrel I can say in about forty seconds and then we'll be down to what we can see for ourselves. So listen to the forty seconds.
cues.through: "Then take the other ten as a gift."
cues.reason: Establishes Rook's controlled authority and the sterile nature of his knowledge.

cues.delivery: Rook explains the plan with absolute certainty. The rhythm should be steady and instructional.
cues.from: "Two and a half miles," he said. "There is a made road running straight up the middle of this bottom to the gate of that place, and we are not going to put one boot on it."
cues.through: "I go two hundred yards west of the orchard, in the open, on my own," said Rook, "because I'm the loud one, and because a thing that goes toward worked power is a thing you can put in a place you'd rather it was."
cues.reason: Maintains the tactical briefing tone as Rook maps out the route.

cues.delivery: Toren's interruption is level and surprising. Do not rush; let the 'No' land as a factual objection.
cues.reason: Marks the first shift in power dynamics from Rook to Toren.

cues.delivery: Toren's speech is dry and precise. He quotes Rook back to him without anger, just cold logic.
cues.from: "You said nobody in this group is bait." Toren's mouth had gone dry. "You said it at a stone heap and you said it in an engine house. You made Milo say it back to you word for word about nine hours before he died. You said if you ever decided otherwise you'd say it out loud to our faces beforehand, and we could tell you what we thought of it."
cues.through: "I think it's the arch again," said Toren. "I think it's you going up a road on your own at three in the morning at a third of the room, because it's the only plan. I think you're at a quarter this morning and not a third. And I think the last time we did this we came back down the bank with four people."
cues.reason: Highlights the intellectual nature of Toren's challenge.

cues.delivery: Rook responds with a weary acceptance. The admission of error regarding Milo must feel heavy but not melodramatic.
cues.from: "No, let him," said Rook. "He's got it in order and he's saying it to my face in front of everybody. That's exactly what the arrangement was for." He crouched down on his heels, which cost him. "Here's my answer and you're owed it plainly. I'm not bait. Bait is a thing you leave somewhere. I'm the loudest thing in this basin whether I stand here or two hundred yards west, and there is no version of this morning where that thing does not know where I am. The only question available is whether I am standing beside that cart when it arrives, or two hundred yards away from it."
cues.through: "And if you'd like a thing to hold," Rook added, getting up, "hold this. Milo was right on the Level and I was wrong. I have had eleven days to find the place where he was wrong, and there isn't one. That is not going to make me hand a road to a child. It has made me a great deal more careful about which of us is standing where."
cues.reason: Shows Rook's vulnerability without breaking his character.

cues.delivery: Narrative description of the creature. Keep it clinical and observational; avoid horror-movie tropes.
cues.from: Then the sound came across two hundred yards of open ground. It was the first sound any of them ever heard that thing make, and it was not a noise an animal makes.
cues.through: Toren stood in an orchard row with an ugly grey hook coming off the back of his own knuckles and looked at a thing the exact same colour, and something in him went a long way down and did not come back up for a week.
cues.reason: Establishes the threat through detail rather than emotion.

cues.delivery: Rook's commands are sharp and urgent. The shout is a tactical necessity.
cues.through: "GO!" he shouted. "Wyck, straight up the row, don't look at it —"
cues.reason: Captures the immediate danger of the encounter.

cues.delivery: Toren's internal realization. The pacing should slow to reflect his confusion and the speed of the event.
cues.from: Toren's first model of that thing was wrong. It was a reasonable model, and he had been given it himself on a towpath above a dry canal by a man with a hazel rod.
cues.through: "NOT THE STOP," Rook shouted from the grass. "The stop is the OTHER ONE — get the cart OFF this row —"
cues.reason: Contrasts Toren's mental processing with the physical chaos.

cues.delivery: Rook shouting from the ground. The urgency is palpable but not hysterical.
cues.from: They did not get the cart off that row.
cues.reason: Emphasizes the critical failure of Rook's plan.

cues.delivery: Toren's action is described with a detached clarity. The realization that the creature didn't see him should feel cold.
cues.through: That was what he could not get past, afterward. It had not even known he was there. It had gone because it was going, in a straight line, the way it did, and he had been off the line.
cues.reason: Highlights Toren's confusion and lack of agency.

cues.delivery: The aftermath description. The tone is somber and factual.
cues.from: Here is what it cost them to get four hundred and sixty yards into a dead orchard.
cues.through: Dessa did the Reading at about nine o'clock, sitting in broken glass, with two fingers above his wrist.
cues.reason: Establishes the cost of the encounter.

cues.delivery: Dessa's reading is quiet and precise. The fraction 'An eighth' should land with finality.
cues.through: "That's about what I've got as well. Good." He got himself up onto one elbow against the brick footing. "Now everybody stop looking at me, because I am going to be no use to any of you inside an hour and we have about that long to become a group that does not need me."
cues.reason: Confirms the severity of Rook's injury.

cues.delivery: Toren's analysis. The rhythm should be deliberate as he pieces together the creature's mechanics.
cues.from: "It stopped," he said. "Twice. Both times it stopped first and then it cut. I went at it on a stop because a stop is four seconds and a stop is where you go. And it wasn't four seconds. It was —" He shook his head. "It wasn't anything. It was less than a blink."
cues.reason: Shows Toren shifting from victim to analyst.

cues.delivery: Dessa's confirmation. Her voice is flat and authoritative.
cues.reason: Solidifies the new understanding of the creature.

cues.delivery: Toren's realization. The pacing should slow as he grasps the 'hole' in the creature.
cues.from: Toren sat in the glass and felt the thing arrive in him whole, the way the number of a distance arrives, without being asked for.
cues.through: "Half a second," said Dessa Cole, in the voice she used for reading out the number of crows in an elm. "It's half a second. I've had eleven of them and they're all the same and I'd put money on it in a yard."

cues.delivery: Rook's admission of failure. The tone is weary and resigned.
cues.through: They tested it at ten o'clock. It worked. It did not help at all.

cues.delivery: Rook lays out the bad plan. The delivery is flat and matter-of-fact.
cues.from: "We've got the tell and the tell is a good one and Dessa can call it in a voice that carries. That buys us one thing and I want everybody to be clear about what the one thing is. It lets us not be hit.
cues.reason: Emphasizes the hopelessness of the situation.

cues.delivery: Toren's final declaration. The 'No' is firm and decisive.
cues.from: "There is no afterward in it," said Elias Marsh. "That's what makes it the only one."
cues.through: "No," he said. "I've got a better one."
cues.reason: Ends the scene with a shift in agency.
